figures.finding: Brunei levies no income tax on individuals: the Income Tax Act charges a person other than a company at the rates of its Schedule 2, and Schedule 2 sets no rate.

sources.said: There shall be levied and paid for each year of assessment upon the chargeable income of every person, other than a company, tax at the rates specified in Schedule 2.
RATE OF TAX ON CHARGEABLE INCOME Chargeable Income Rate of Tax LAWS OF BRUNEI Income Tax CAP. 35 141 SCHEDULE 3
Brunei does not impose personal income tax on individuals.
Although the Income Tax Act provides for the taxation of income derived by individuals, such income is exempt from tax under the second schedule of the act.

figures.finding: A Brunei citizen or permanent resident pays 8.5% of basic salary to the National Retirement Scheme (SPK); the employer pays BND 57.50 a month on salary up to BND 500, 10.5% to BND 1,500, 9.5% to BND 2,800 and 8.5% above.
figures.applies: From July 2023; citizens and permanent residents only, so a foreign screen worker pays none. A self-employed scheme was not found.

sources.said: SPK applies to citizens and permanent residents of Brunei only. Under this scheme, the employee’s contribution rate is 8.5% from the basic salary

The employer contribution rates are BND 57.50 (for a monthly salary up to BND 500), 10.5% (for a monthly salary above BND 500 and up to BND 1,500), 9.5% (for a monthly salary above BND 1,500 and up to BND 2,800), and 8.5% (for a monthly salary above BND 2,800).

figures.finding: No income tax is withheld from pay in Brunei; withholding applies only to certain payments to non-residents.

sources.said: Brunei does not impose personal income tax on individuals.

figures.finding: A non-resident individual performing in Brunei owes no income tax on the fee; withholding of 10% applies only to listed payments to non-residents (royalties, technical and management fees, a non-resident director's remuneration, rent of movable property).
figures.applies: A royalty paid to a non-resident writer or director bears 10% unless a treaty reduces it.

figures.finding: Brunei has no VAT or sales tax, so a freelancer's fee bears none.
